name: Social Libertarianism
summary: Social libertarianism, as the catalog's Wikipedia match treats it, is left-libertarianism: it combines strong personal liberty and self-ownership with an egalitarian claim on natural resources. Adherents hold that appropriating land and resources obliges owners to compensate everyone else, which supports resource-rent taxes, inheritance levies and a universal basic income. They defend markets and civil liberties, oppose war, border controls and nationalism, and distrust a state that serves dominant groups.
scope: The mainstream left-libertarian family: the distributive tradition (Hillel Steiner, Peter Vallentyne, Michael Otsuka, Philippe Van Parijs) descending from Paine's Agrarian Justice and Henry George, plus the anti-capitalist free-market strand (Chartier, Long, Carson). Social-anarchist and Bookchin-style municipalist strands are noted but not treated as the core, and many answers on modern issues are inferred.

keyFigures.name: Hillel Steiner
keyFigures.role: Philosopher whose theory ties self-ownership to equal claims on natural resources and a basic income.

keyFigures.name: Thomas Paine
keyFigures.role: Author of Agrarian Justice, an early proposal to pay each person from rent owed for land.

keyFigures.name: Philippe Van Parijs
keyFigures.role: Philosopher and advocate of an unconditional basic income as real freedom for all.

sources.title: Left-libertarianism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Strands, welfare, basic income, decentralisation, social anarchist and free-market currents.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Left-libertarians back redistribution and welfare provision, so a guaranteed health entitlement is inferred, though many would deliver it as cash rather than state-run care.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage floors override voluntary contracts, so adherents prefer income support from resource rents; inferred from that preference for a basic income over market rules.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Both strands defend free markets, the distributive strand pairing them with a resource tax and the radical strand with abolition of state privilege.

public-ownership.rationale: Industries are not natural resources, and the state is distrusted as unconsented and captured by dominant groups, so adherents do not want it owning them.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Resource-rent and inheritance levies fall mostly on the rich, but the principle is compensation for resource claims, not a general soak-the-rich aim; inferred.

unions-good.rationale: Anti-capitalist left-libertarians sympathise with voluntary worker organising, but sources say little on unions; inferred.

property-fundamental.rationale: Private appropriation of natural resources is conditional on compensating everyone else, so ownership of resources is not an inviolable right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The radical strand wants state privileges removed rather than regulation while the distributive strand would accept regulation; adherents are split.

cut-welfare.rationale: Many left-libertarians favour state welfare or a basic income, so they reject the dependency argument, though the radical strand wants it market-delivered.

worker-ownership.rationale: Social anarchists want collective ownership, while market left-libertarians and the distributive strand leave ownership forms to voluntary choice; adherents are split.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The state's monopoly of force is seen as dangerous and self-ownership grounds privacy against it, so terrorism does not justify mass surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Self-ownership gives a principled objection to paternalism, so adults may use what they choose.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: They oppose racism and sexism but as liberty-first thinkers distrust giving the state power to punish speech.

strong-leader.rationale: A leader bypassing checks embodies the concentrated, unconsented state power that left-libertarians distrust.

state-harmful.rationale: The radical strand holds the state inherently unjust, but the distributive strand relies on a state to collect rents and pay a basic income; adherents are split.

limit-guns.rationale: Strict limits expand state coercive power over persons, but adherents' views are not documented; inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: The state's monopoly on force is seen as a danger serving dominant groups, so more power for police and army runs against the core view.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Sexual liberation and self-ownership entail legal commerce between consenting adults.

decide-locally.rationale: Left-libertarian forms range from decentralised, participatory government to municipal confederation.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not documented in sources; inferred from emancipatory, anti-punitive leanings and suspicion of state coercion.

traditional-family.rationale: They oppose sexism and champion personal autonomy over inherited forms; inferred from that.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Left-libertarians are described as opposing homophobia as part of emancipation, though some would end state marriage altogether.

abortion-legal.rationale: Self-ownership of one's body is the core principle, which supports control over pregnancy.

more-religion-public.rationale: Sources note libertarian cultural and religious freedom, not a stance on public religion; inferred from their opposition to state paternalism.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Adherents oppose racism and favour rectifying unjust holdings, but sources do not discuss racial redress policy; inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Left-libertarians oppose sexism but the theory does not take a side on the nature of gender.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: They are described as opposing nationalism as part of human emancipation.

gradual-change.rationale: Strands range from radical anarchist to reformist redistributive; adherents are split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Libertarianism opposes border restrictions and left-libertarians oppose nationalism.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Wary of concentrated state power, though sources do not discuss international bodies; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Libertarians oppose border restrictions and the radical strand backs free markets while opposing state-favoured corporations.

nation-first.rationale: Left-libertarians are described as opposing nationalism.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Libertarians generally oppose war, and the state's force is seen as serving dominant groups.

open-borders.rationale: Libertarianism opposes border restrictions, and the left strands extend equal claims to all persons.

limit-growth.rationale: Green-left currents are called left-libertarian, but sources show no consensus on growth limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Resource-use taxes fit but the call for drastic state action conflicts with state distrust; adherents are split.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No documented position; ideology is neutral on technology.

expand-nuclear.rationale: No documented position; green-aligned and market strands differ.

revolution-justified.rationale: Social anarchists accept revolution while the distributive strand is reformist; adherents are split.

experts-over-public.rationale: Individual autonomy and anti-paternalism imply distrust of expert rule; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Both strands defend free markets and treat state economic direction as favouring incumbents.

socialized-markets.rationale: Some strands favour worker or cooperative ownership but not as a condition for markets; adherents are split.

land-value-tax.rationale: Henry George-style taxes on the natural value of land are a named left-libertarian option, though replacing most taxes goes beyond what all accept.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Paine proposed a tax on property passing at death to fund payments to all, an ancestor of the position.

basic-income.rationale: The SEP ties Steiner's egalitarian resource claims to a universal basic income, and Widerquist and Van Parijs defend one.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Libertarian opposition to border restrictions and to state favours to incumbents rules out protection.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Existing capitalism is seen as the product of state intervention on behalf of incumbents, so more direction is rejected.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Paine wanted the land monopoly broken so people share in inheritance, and the individualist-anarchist roots favour dispersed ownership.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Only social anarchists seek it; the mainstream defends markets; inferred as minority view.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Market-anarchist strand likes it; the distributive strand has no stance; adherents are split.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies setting wages and prices contradict free markets and distrust of state privilege.

one-party-rule.rationale: Rule by a single party is the antithesis of consent-based, liberty-first politics.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Paine's attack on hereditary privilege and the consent standard exclude hereditary rule.

democracy-best.rationale: Participatory democracy is favoured, but majority rule is limited by individual rights; sources not specific.

direct-votes.rationale: Bookchin-style direct democracy and participatory government appear in the family; majority of strands not documented.

workers-councils.rationale: Council communism appears only among social anarchists; inferred as a minority view.

right-to-secede.rationale: The state is held unjust without consent, so exit by regions follows.

natural-rulers.rationale: Equal self-ownership and the consent standard reject natural hierarchy.

political-violence-never.rationale: Defensive force is accepted by libertarians, while many reject all political violence; adherents are split.

war-builds-character.rationale: Opposition to war and state violence is a standard libertarian position.

separate-church-state.rationale: Religious freedom and opposition to paternalism imply separation; sources do not address it directly.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Imposing religious law on adults is the paternalism libertarians object to.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Market anarchists favour it but distributive strands rely on a state; adherents are split.

military-superiority.rationale: Libertarian opposition to war and the state's force excludes arms-race goals.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Social anarchists agree while market left-libertarians do not; adherents are split.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Steiner-style views equalise claims on natural resources, not final outcomes, which stay with individuals' choices and labour.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Egalitarian resource claims and anti-colonial leanings support it, but sources do not cover it; inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Rectification of unjust holdings applies in principle but sources do not address states; adherents are split.

civilizational-union.rationale: Opposition to nationalism and to larger states implies rejection; inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Libertarians defend freedom to pursue interests but left strands stress social equality; adherents are split.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Rights inhere in self-owning individuals, not in community duties.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Green currents hold it; the doctrine itself does not.

limit-population.rationale: State coercion over reproduction conflicts with self-ownership; inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Self-ownership implies freedom over one's body; inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Delegating decisions to the state apparatus cuts against distrust of it and participatory ideals; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Distrust of the state's monopoly of force supports private communication.

restore-past-order.rationale: The family is emancipatory and rejects hierarchical past orders.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Principled justice claims are central, so results alone do not decide; inferred.

direct-action.rationale: Anarchist roots favour it, while reformists use elections; inferred majority.

means-match-ends.rationale: Prefigurative thinking is found in Bookchin's tradition; not documented across the family.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Rare fringe within green anarchism; inferred.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Entitlements come from self-ownership and shares of natural resources, not need.

production-for-use.rationale: Social anarchists agree while market strands accept profit; adherents are split.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The radical strand sees profit as flowing from state privilege, the distributive strand does not; adherents are split.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Dictatorial power is opposed on liberty and consent grounds.

collective-farming.rationale: Paine and the individualist heritage favour individual property in cultivation; inferred rejection of compelled collectivisation.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The radical strand blames state-capital partnership but the distributive strand does not; adherents are split.

taxation-theft.rationale: Right-libertarians reason this way, but left-libertarians justify taxation as compensation for resource claims; the radical strand sometimes agrees.

harm-principle.rationale: Self-ownership's objection to paternalism yields the view that only harm to others justifies restriction.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Self-ownership makes rights individual, though some egalitarian claims are held by all persons.

conscription.rationale: Conscription violates self-ownership, the core principle.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Consent and secession matter but voting remains valued by participatory strands; adherents are split.

state-as-business.rationale: Customer framing neglects equal resource claims; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Van Parijs and Widerquist defend an income large enough to give real independence.

media-academia-power.rationale: No documented claim; inferred from state-focused power analysis.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Left-libertarians oppose racism but empirical claim is not addressed; inferred.

organic-representation.rationale: Corporatist representation conflicts with individualism, though local confederal forms are favoured; inferred.

total-state.rationale: A state directing every area of life is the opposite of the view.

national-rebirth.rationale: Rebirth myths belong to nationalism, which they oppose.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Expansionism is rejected through opposition to war and nationalism.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Paine's critique of hereditary and arbitrary authority excludes it.

universal-morality.rationale: Natural-rights reasoning from self-ownership assumes universal moral claims; sources do not state it for the family.

single-common-good.rationale: Individual rights and pluralism are central; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Opposition to nationalism and unconsented states implies rejection of state-founding claims; inferred.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Ethnic criteria for citizenship are rejected; inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: State-imposed language policy is rejected; inferred.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Many left-libertarians favour democratic firms; not stated across the family.

school-vouchers.rationale: Choice-based public funding fits market and basic-income approaches; inferred.

economic-freedom.rationale: Left-libertarians defend free markets as freedom, though not as a sufficient condition; inferred.

rule-by-example.rationale: Paine relied on law and consent, not rulers' virtue; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Consent supports self-rule but nationalism is opposed; adherents are split.

force-without-un.rationale: Opposition to war excludes unauthorised force.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Border restrictions are opposed and resource claims are universal.

work-for-welfare.rationale: A basic income is unconditional, not tied to work.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Destroying institutions by state fiat is coercive; inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: Bloc politics rests on nationalism; inferred.

workers-nation.rationale: National organising conflicts with anti-nationalism; inferred.

ban-interest.rationale: Legal bans interfere with voluntary contracts; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: They oppose racism and state coercion.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The radical strand sees the state as serving dominant groups, though the distributive strand is less critical.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Cultural freedom and opposition to nationalism exclude compelled assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiratorial claim contradicts their pro-immigration stance.

national-mission.rationale: Missions to spread a government oppose anti-nationalism and anti-war views.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: They oppose sexism as oppression, but the structural claim is not documented in sources.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: State capture by dominant groups is a core claim; this populist wording is inferred.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: State control over reproduction violates self-ownership.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Left-libertarians reject confining government to Nozickian minimal functions; the state or association collects resource rents.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Left-libertarians are described as opposing racism, and choosing partners is a matter of personal liberty, so social or legal discouragement is rejected.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equal self-ownership and equal shares of natural resources express equal worth.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: No documented position on this framing.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Equality before law versus pluralism; adherents are split.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Cultural and religious freedom is libertarian.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: State-funded religion conflicts with neutrality; inferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The SEP says left-libertarians consider the state inherently unjust because it is not consented to.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilism conflicts with free trade and opposition to state favours.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal of a minority violates self-ownership and the opposition to nationalism.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Non-aggression is the shared foundation of libertarian justice.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social Darwinist framing is opposed; inferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Restrictions on association are distrusted; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Concern with domination by powerful groups matches, but formulation not documented.

separated-powers.rationale: Fits distrust of concentrated power; inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: Disciplined party leadership contradicts liberty and consent.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Basic-income and leximin arguments emphasise the worst off; inferred for stated priority.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Restricting voluntary action is disliked, but sources say little; inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Paine says poverty is created by civilisation's land monopoly and not by nature, placing its cause in institutions.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Civil liberties are central and not suspendable.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party control of arms opposes civil liberty.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Internal religious governance is indifferent to the state view.

clerical-rule.rationale: Clerical rule is paternalism and unconsented authority.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Bans on voluntary contracts are opposed.

people-in-arms.rationale: Distrust of state monopoly versus anti-militarism; adherents are split.

death-penalty.rationale: State killing is opposed by distrust of state force; inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Liberty fits exemptions but sources silent; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Cultural freedom and sexual liberation are named libertarian values.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Equal claims on natural resources extend globally, since all persons share them.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property is conditional on compensation, but common-good justification is not the standard; adherents are split.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Anti-authoritarian socialists made this critique; family-wide stance inferred.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliances are opposed by anti-war stance; inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: State coercion over religion is opposed; inferred.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Consent is central and the state is held unjust without it.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Paine's attack on hereditary rule excludes it.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Left-libertarian taxes are resource-based and redistributive; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Rulers answer to consent and law.

leader-cult.rationale: Personality cults conflict with anti-state and anti-authoritarian values.

land-redistribution.rationale: Paine explicitly distinguished his ground-rent plan from taking land from owners (Agrarian Law).

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Penalising someone for leaving a religion is the kind of paternalism and coercion over personal belief that libertarians reject.

ban-cartels.rationale: Radical strand removes privileges rather than trust-busting; adherents are split.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts exemplify state interventions favouring incumbents.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarky opposes free trade and anti-nationalism.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Paine's work attacked hereditary privilege; inferred for titles.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Imperial tutelage violates equal self-ownership and consent.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: No documented position; adherents are split.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Imperial influence opposed by anti-war stance; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Freedom of association competes with opposition to racism; adherents are split.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Rights against government are central; inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: Paine rejected hereditary succession in favour of consent.

minority-veto.rationale: Consent is central but is unworkable as stated; adherents are split.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Consent implies right to resist; inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Duty by privilege is paternalistic, but redistributive duty fits; adherents are split.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Equal rights regardless of descent; inferred.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Slavery is the clearest violation of self-ownership; inferred for this historical claim.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Military politics is a danger of state force.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Personal autonomy and opposition to state control over private life.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Some accept usufruct while others accept taxed private ownership; adherents are split.

single-official-language.rationale: Opposition to state coercion over culture.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Funding foreign insurgents is state war-making, which libertarians oppose and which serves dominant groups' interests.

corporate-influence.rationale: The radical strand holds that capitalism results from state interventions favouring incumbents.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The state is held inherently unjust because unconsented.

non-intervention.rationale: No documented position; defense of persons may justify force.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Left-libertarians oppose racism and nationalism, so a conspiracy narrative about a minority is rejected.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: State role in marriage is doubted; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: Defining the national community by religion rests on the nationalism these thinkers oppose and ignores equal individual rights.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Equal claims on resources across persons; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Personal property is accepted by all strands; inferred.

defeat-communism.rationale: The statement frames a goal of state confrontation, which cuts against the anti-war stance; left-libertarians would favour coexistence, though some are anti-communist.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Voluntary communities are allowed, but mandated reorganisation is not; adherents are split.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The radical strand opposes capitalism but defends markets; inferred.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Natural resources are claimed equally; inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Factual claim; not addressed in sources.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Sexual liberty is a core value.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Suppressing opposition violates the civil liberties at the heart of libertarianism and the state's consent requirement.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Participatory forms are cited in left-libertarian traditions.

assisted-dying.rationale: Self-ownership implies a right; not documented.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The label fuses left and libertarian elements; inferred.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Liberty implies people may dress as they wish, though some would keep officials of the state neutral; inferred as a mild disagreement.

social-market-economy.rationale: Markets plus basic income is the distributive model; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Opposition to war and to the state's monopoly of force points toward disarmament, though sources do not state it for the family; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Staying out of great-power blocs follows from opposing war and military alliances, though sources do not discuss blocs; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: Tying votes to wealth contradicts equal self-ownership and equal moral worth, which left-libertarians treat as basic.

racial-franchise.rationale: Restricting the vote by race contradicts their opposition to racism and equal rights of persons.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Adults choosing whom to marry is a matter of personal liberty, so legal limits on interfaith marriage are rejected.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Left-libertarians oppose racism and religious prejudice, so organised targeting of a minority's shops is condemned even if technically voluntary.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Concentrations of resource value are the target of resource taxes, and state-business alliances are criticised.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Social anarchists may agree while distributive strands rely on a state; adherents are split.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Redistribution via basic income is preferred; inferred.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Their opposition to sexism favours equal eligibility, though private religious bodies may set their own rules; inferred.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Opposition to sexism implies equal authority between spouses, and marriage is a voluntary contract between equals.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Opposing border restrictions and nationalism leads to treating residents as equal participants wherever they live.

abolish-ip.rationale: Market-anarchist strand yes, distributive no; adherents are split.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Opposition to war and to state military power favours keeping nuclear weapons away, though sources do not address it directly; inferred.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Anti-war views imply hosting no foreign bases, though sources do not discuss basing; inferred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Georgist-style views let workers keep the value they add, while rent from natural resources is shared.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Defence of persons is accepted in libertarian justice; inferred.

municipal-property.rationale: Bookchin favoured municipal ownership but other strands do not; adherents are split.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Bookchin's confederal model is one strand; adherents are split.

person-over-state.rationale: Self-ownership makes persons ends in themselves, not means to state ends.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Rights belong to individuals and racism is opposed.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Steiner-style tax liabilities on appropriated resources fit taxes on resource use.

future-generations.rationale: Otsuka's proviso demands leaving enough and as good for others.

arms-reduction.rationale: Opposition to war and state military power favours smaller arsenals, though sources do not discuss disarmament; inferred.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Distrust of the state monopoly of force; inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Opposition to state wars and conscription supports individual refusal, though sources do not discuss orders; inferred.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Voluntary choice either way; adherents are split.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Radical strand yes, distributive no; adherents are split.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Charging for natural resource value fits; inferred.

sacred-nation.rationale: A sacred nation that outlasts and subordinates its members contradicts individualism and opposition to nationalism.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Left-libertarians distrust the state's weapons and oppose war, so keeping arsenals is disfavoured; inferred rather than documented.

ban-fgm.rationale: Harms a person without consent; inferred.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Left-libertarians oppose sexism, and equal self-ownership implies equal rights to own and inherit property.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Market-anarchist strand favours liability for harms; inferred.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Cutting access is a sweeping state restriction of civil liberties, which libertarians oppose.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Basic-income family; the schemes share cash and phase-out features.

women-suffrage.rationale: Equal self-ownership and opposition to sexism mean women hold the same political rights as men.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The distributive strand rejects pure first-claim and ties appropriation to compensation.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Opposition to sexism favours guaranteeing women's participation, though sources do not discuss indigenous self-government; inferred.

indirect-election.rationale: Confederal strand yes, others no; adherents are split.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Consent of the governed is central, so letting inhabitants decide fits, though sources do not discuss plebiscites; inferred.

equal-conscription.rationale: Conscription is opposed in all forms, which satisfies the 'neither' option; inferred.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: This is the defining claim of distributive left-libertarianism, and no existing statement states it; homestead-ownership only covers the opposing view.

self-ownership.rationale: Self-ownership is the shared foundation of all libertarian justice and the SEP's starting point for the left-libertarian argument.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Left-libertarians distrust nationalism and treat land as a matter of equal claims, so a spiritual national tie is inferred to be rejected.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Left-libertarians defend civil liberties and distrust state power, which excludes killing suspects without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: The strand opposes war and nationalism but has no stated view on great-power alignment.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Left-libertarians oppose nationalism and border controls, so a state favouring its kin abroad is rejected.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Left-libertarians tax resource rents and land values to fund a basic income, so cutting consumption taxes is inferred to fit; not discussed directly.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The distributive tradition pays a universal basic income rather than needs-tested aid, as Paine's and Van Parijs's schemes do.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Left-libertarians favour voluntary association and distrust the state, but not parties as such; inferred, with adherents split.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The strand distrusts a state serving dominant groups and its anti-capitalist free-market wing attacks corporate privilege.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Distrust of state-organised communities and support for individual liberty are inferred to favour cross-denominational politics.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Left-libertarians are neither traditionalist nor technophobic; there is no stated view.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Self-ownership and personal liberty imply a wife may leave a marriage; inferred, as the sources do not discuss divorce.

national-resource-control.rationale: Left-libertarians hold that resources belong to everyone equally, not to one nation; inferred from that and their anti-nationalism.

missingStatements.text: Natural resources belong to everyone equally, so those who appropriate them owe compensation to all others.
missingStatements.rationale: This is the defining claim of distributive left-libertarianism, and no existing statement states it; homestead-ownership only covers the opposing view.

missingStatements.text: Self-ownership gives each person full rights over their own body and labour.
missingStatements.rationale: Self-ownership is the shared foundation of all libertarian justice and the SEP's starting point for the left-libertarian argument.

notes: Catalog entry redirects to Left-libertarianism, where the term covers both an egalitarian-resource tradition and an anti-capitalist market tradition, plus social anarchists. Answers follow the first two; social anarchists would answer differently on property, state, markets and workers' ownership.
